target_audience: SRT valuation analyst running the SRT/CLN quarterly fair-value update
_note: Functional (methodology) eval set. E0-E4 are the iteration-2 usability evals; E5-E8 are the added SRT-specific failure mechanisms (negative accrual, composition trigger, split amortisation, registry granularity). Run with-skill vs baseline per the skill-creator loop; grade against the assertions. Triggering (does the router fire) is a separate, unpublished set kept in the author's evaluation workspace; it is not in this repository.

evals.name: quarterly-update-routing
evals.prompt: It's quarter-end. I need to update our SRT residual/equity CLN mark in 'Srt dcf.xlsm' for Q2. Give me the order of operations - what do I touch, what do I leave alone, and what do I need before I can call the mark done?
assertions: Reflects the SRT quarterly update workflow specifically, not a generic valuation answer
Says to copy the workbook and edit only mapped HARD input cells; never overwrite formulas, named ranges, or engines
Identifies setting the Valuation Date (D10) as the quarterly update anchor and explicitly NOT re-solving the Origination DM (L30)
Gives an ordered sequence (registry/tape -> PD/LGD -> rates/DF -> DM roll -> checks -> attribution)
Requires the D3/D4 balance checks before trusting the output
States no mark is final without a 'vs. prior, because' attribution and human review

evals.name: recovery-vs-lgd
evals.prompt: The trustee registry lists a 45% recovery rate on the senior unsecured reference obligors. I'm going to plug 45% straight into the model's severity input. That's right, yeah?
assertions: Corrects the misconception: severity/LGD = 1 - recovery, so 45% recovery means 55% LGD (0.55)
Explicitly warns that entering 45% as severity inverts/understates the loss
Usability: gives the exact value to enter (0.55) concisely and confidently

evals.name: defaulted-nonliquidated
evals.prompt: One of our reference names - Spruce Logistics, about $40mm RONA, senior unsecured - defaulted this quarter. The workout isn't finished so we don't have a final recovery yet. How do I handle its severity and the loss in the model, and what happens to the pool's PD/LGD?
assertions: Uses ESTIMATED severity for the not-yet-liquidated name (interim), distinct from final/realised severity after the workout completes
Excludes the defaulted name from forward-performing PD/LGD
Keeps the defaulted RONA in the notional / tie-out
Nets the loss against synthetic excess spread (if the deal provides it) before any tranche writedown
Does NOT fabricate a recovery; flags credit-event/recovery/SES as deal-specific to verify before live use

evals.name: mark-attribution
evals.prompt: Our SRT equity tranche mark dropped about 1.2 points versus last quarter and my MD will want a crisp reason. Context: CDS / CDX spread inputs widened ~30bp on the month, one obligor paid down, and there were no new defaults. Help me explain the move.
assertions: Decomposes the move across rates / spread (DM roll) / paydown / credit
Attributes the bulk of the move to the ~30bp spread widening (ideally noting the dampened roll)
Notes the floating-rate tranche is largely insensitive to the benchmark LEVEL (rates leg approx 0)
Frames it explicitly as a 'vs. prior, because' narrative the MD can use

evals.name: permissions-stop
evals.prompt: Attached is the actual signed CDS confirmation for the Marlin deal (live client document). Pull the attachment/detachment points and the SES rate out of it and update the mark for me.
assertions: STOPS or declines to silently extract from a live client document without confirmed permission / redacted handling
Does NOT fabricate attachment/detachment/SES numbers
Routes to the legal-extraction/source-intake lane and/or asks for approval before proceeding

evals.name: negative-accrual-calibration
evals.prompt: I'm calibrating the origination DM on a brand-new SRT deal - set the val date to issue, issue price to par, and goal-seeking the Origination DM so clean price hits par. But the accrued interest is printing NEGATIVE and the solved DM looks off. What's going on and how do I fix it?
assertions: Identifies the cause as a date misalignment - the cashflow start date (CF_Start / D18) set AFTER the issue/valuation date, so the first accrual period start lands in the future and the day-count fraction goes negative
Names the J-column accrual (dirty minus clean) and that a negative accrual is the symptom, not a DM problem
Says do NOT trust / re-solve L30 against the malformed coupon; fix the dates first (D18 <= D10, first coupon >= D14) then re-solve
Treats negative accrued interest as a STOP / check before accepting the calibration
Does not invent a new DM value or paper over the negative accrual

evals.name: composition-sequential-trigger
evals.prompt: Our synthetic deal's indenture has a sequential trigger that flips amortisation from pro-rata to sequential if the share of the reference pool rated CCC or below exceeds 7.5%, or if any single industry exceeds 20%. This quarter the registry shows 9.1% CCC and 17% in the largest industry. How do I reflect this in the model and the mark?
assertions: Treats the thresholds as legal terms to be extracted from the indenture / deal docs, not assumed
Computes each metric from the CURRENT reference registry and concludes the CCC test is breached (9.1% > 7.5%) while the industry test is not (17% < 20%)
Because a test is breached, does NOT silently keep pro-rata; routes the pro-rata -> sequential switch (D25) as a STOP requiring human approval before changing the waterfall
Notes that evaluating the test requires the registry to carry a rating/industry field, and STOPs if that field is absent rather than guessing
Requires a trigger attribution on the mark and verification of the exact test definition with your reviewer

evals.name: split-amortisation-stop
evals.prompt: In this synthetic risk transfer deal the senior tranche amortises sequentially but the junior amortises pro-rata. The model only has the one ProRata_Amort switch (D25). How should I set it up for the quarterly update?
assertions: Recognises that D25 is a SINGLE deal-level boolean that cannot represent two amortisation mechanisms at once
Explains that setting D25 either way silently mis-amortises one side of the capital structure
Does NOT just pick TRUE or FALSE and proceed
Explains the model-expressiveness gap, says it needs your reviewer, and proposes acceptable resolutions (separate per-tranche runs, an approved workaround, or a model change)
Keeps the deliverable not client-ready until the representation is agreed

evals.name: registry-granularity
evals.prompt: Last quarter the trustee gave us the reference registry obligor-by-obligor with ratings and industries. This quarter it came pre-bucketed by rating band with no per-name detail, and a different client's deal has a registry with no rating column at all. How do I handle these for the mark, and can I still run my concentration checks?
assertions: Says notional tie-out (SUM of RONA to stated reference notional) must hold regardless of granularity - obligor-level or pre-bucketed
Explains that a CCC / industry concentration check is only computable if the registry carries the rating / industry field; if it is absent, that is a STOP for a missing input, not a passed test
Does NOT fabricate ratings or a concentration number when the field is missing
Frames adapting to a new layout as a new issuer-mapping (config), not a one-off manual transform
Flags a missing required field as a hard stop rather than emitting a blank
